title: Bezdek's axial-symmetry conjecture for plane sections of convex bodies
statement: Let $K\subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a convex body. A plane section means the intersection of $K$ with an affine plane, and an **axis of symmetry** is a line in that plane whose reflection preserves the section. **Bezdek's conjecture.** If all plane sections of $K$ have an axis of symmetry, then $K$ is an ellipsoid or a body of revolution. This conjecture asks whether axial symmetry of every plane section forces one of these global forms; the supplied source gives no resolution status.
source_name: Efrén Morales-Amaya, “Convex bodies with sections with hyperplanes of symmetry”, arXiv:2509.17326 (2025).
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2501.06337](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.06337), [arXiv:2307.09585](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.09585).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.17326

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).
